region: Sagaponack · The Hamptons, Long Island, New York
about: Fatalis Fatum belongs to Wölffer’s White Horse series, the estate’s top tier, in which each wine is named for a horse from the Wölffer Estate Stables in Sagaponack. The name translates roughly as “the decision is final,” which winemaker Roman Roth considered fitting for a decisive blend. The estate itself was founded in 1988 by Christian Wölffer on old potato fields near the Atlantic and is run today by his children, Marc and Joey.

It is a Bordeaux-style red built on Merlot, with Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon. White Horse wines are hand-harvested by vineyard manager Richie Pisacano’s team; in past vintages each variety was fermented separately with daily punch-downs, then aged about 20 months in French oak barriques before blending. The result is made for the cellar: Roth describes a red with longevity written all over it.

In the glass, Wölffer’s notes describe deep purple color, ripe cassis and raspberry with an inky, iodine note, classic minerality, toasted oak and roasted nuts, with velvety tannins and a chalky freshness. The winery recommends decanting for at least an hour and pairing it with lamb, game or wild mushroom risotto. Both James Suckling and Wine Enthusiast gave the 2020 92 points.
facts: Merlot-led Bordeaux blend with Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon
French oak barriques (about 20 months in past vintages)
Hand-harvested estate fruit, sustainably certified vineyard
